title: Studio RLS editor rates a non-lowerable USING predicate a WARNING ("can … WIDEN access") and autosaves it, while publish / os build refuse it as an error (rls-predicate-unenforceable, fail-closed)

Filed on behalf of the QA runner session `session_01NvpZQ6sRwAVRNDi4UsF2c7` (its GitHub scope did not include this repository) by the 18.0 QA wave dispatch session `session_01CfRDy7SuTfUqaTu2AEH2Hi`.

## What is wrong
For an RLS USING predicate that cannot be lowered to a row filter — e.g. `size(record.asset_code) > 3` — the Studio editor and the engine give different verdicts for the same expression at the same site:
- **Editor** (objectui `celAuthoring.ts` `lintCelPredicate`, at `4016370a`): `severity: 'warning'` (`engine.celLint.notPushdownable`) with the text that the predicate "can be dropped and WIDEN access"; because it is only a warning the Save gate stays open and the policy autosaves (draft PUT 200).
- **Engine** (`@objectstack/lint` `rls-predicate-unenforceable`, `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts` in objectstack-ai/objectstack, the rule `os build` runs): severity **error**; publish answers **422 `INVALID_METADATA`**, "RLS using is not lowerable (unsupported operand "call"), so the policy is dropped and grants no access".

The editor's wording also states the wrong direction: the runtime fails CLOSED (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts` in objectstack-ai/objectstack adds no filter for a dropped policy and returns the deny filter when none compiles), so a dropped policy only removes the access it was written to grant — it never widens. Not an access-control hole; a second grammar in the GUI, which ADR-0032 / celAuthoring exists to prevent.

## Reproduction
1. Boot the showcase with the console built at the `.objectui-sha` pin; sign in as admin.
2. Create a writable scratch package (`POST /api/v1/packages`) with an object carrying a text field `asset_code`.
3. Studio → that package → Access → a permission set → RLS policy on the object, USING `size(record.asset_code) > 3`.
   - Expected (engine verdict): an error that holds Save, worded as fail-closed ("the policy is dropped and grants no access").
   - Actual: an advisory warning "…can be dropped and WIDEN access"; autosave issues `PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/NAME?package=PKG&mode=draft` → 200.
4. Publish: `POST /api/v1/meta/permission/NAME/publish?package=PKG` → 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, rule `rls-predicate-unenforceable`, severity `error`.
Control: USING `record.asset_code == 'A1'` → no warning; publish 200.

## Expected fix shape
Give the lowerability verdict at error tier for USING and CHECK, using the same decision function the lint rule uses (`isSupportedRlsExpression`), so Save is gated; drop the "WIDEN access" wording in favour of the fail-closed sentence the engine prints.

Note for the checklist lane (not this card's work): the item's own acceptance[2] / acceptance[4] still encode the warning tier and will need the matching re-point; it is recorded on the wave anchor objectstack-ai/objectstack#24579.
